title: First time truly vibe coding and made a zero-gravity fps
author: CaptainAlexWest
selftext: I wanted to try claude code for fun. Set it all up then I fully vibe coded and cooked up this. Then last night I got multplayer player working. Now I'm planning a website.

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: I didn't know that existed. I got to add that.

replies.author: eugene20
replies.body: Descent, Pyrotechnia, Descent 2, were classic low gravity shooters. Any floaty shooter with simple/preproduction graphics would be hard pressed to not be reminiscent of those  :)

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: Thanks for telling me all those. It's funny that all the old classic games look like the vibe coded games now. 🤣

comments.author: smokalone
comments.body:
Nice work!
May i ask you more details? How long does it takes? What tools did you used?

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: This took like 4 hours. I didn't know what I was doing. I used claude code in the powershell terminal and Microsoft edge. I'm using three.js and node.js because it runs on the browser and a potato computer. Now I'm in VScode. I got multplayer working and game structure. Now, I am debating on building out a website and deploying. If I had a problem or error I talked to claude.

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: It took like 4 hours. I used claude code and Microsoft edge. Now I'm on vs code.

comments.author: shekyb
comments.body: recoil from the gun should propel the player back in 0 gravity, right?

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: Yeah, I was thinking that, too. I got to add it and make the player explode like the robots. Thanks for reminding me.

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: I made claude chat do a scaffolding, and then loaded up claude code. I just kept fixing stuff that I didn't like and fixing bugs. 4 hours later, then came out.
